chunks: 33. Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, on the authority of a number of them, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He who compares Allah with His creation is an associate (polytheist), and he who denies His Omnipotence is a disbeliever.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between shirk and kufr in the context of comparing God to creation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to delineate the boundary between *Shirk* (associating partners with God) and *Kufr* (disbelief) by linking them to specific theological errors: anthropomorphism (*Tashbih*) and denial of divine omnipotence (*Inkar al-Qudra*). In Shia scholarship, this serves as a foundational criterion for *Tawhid al-Sifat*, emphasizing that while God’s attributes are real, they must be understood without likening them to created beings or limiting His absolute power.
